summary.text: Clyde Vanel is the Democratic incumbent for Assembly District 33 in southeast Queens. An attorney, entrepreneur and pilot, he lost a first bid for the seat in 2012 and won it in 2016. He chairs the Assembly Banks Committee and its Subcommittee on Internet and New Technology, focuses on emerging-technology legislation, and is running for re-election after winning the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, Vanel was raised in Cambria Heights, Queens, with nine siblings.

He holds a Bachelor of Science in Aviation Administration and an Associate of Applied Science in Aerospace Technology from Farmingdale State College, where he was Student Government President, and a Juris Doctor from Boston University School of Law, where he was Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of Science & Technology Law.

He owns and operates Vanel Law Firm, P.C., where he practices intellectual property and business law, and runs TrademarkReady.com, a trademark-filing service. He previously owned and operated a restaurant and lounge, Vanel on First, in Lower Manhattan for five years.
Vanel also founded the New York Metro chapter of Black Pilots of America, Inc., which trains and exposes community members and youth to aviation, and is a member of the MIT AI Policy Forum.
Vanel first ran for Assembly District 33 in 2012, losing the Democratic primary to incumbent Barbara M. Clark and then losing to her in the general election on the More Jobs Party line.

He won the 2016 Democratic primary for the open seat and the general election, and his official biography dates his service to his November 8, 2016 election; he took office in 2017. The district includes Cambria Heights, St. Albans, Hollis, Queens Village, Bellerose, and parts of Floral Park.
He has defeated Oster Bryan in Democratic primaries in 2018, 2020 and 2022, and again won the 2026 Democratic primary.

In the 2025-2026 session Vanel chairs the Banks Committee and the Subcommittee on Internet and New Technology, and is a member of the Codes, Racing and Wagering, Rules, and Science & Technology committees, the Black Task Force, and the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus.

His official biography says he has sponsored legislation to create a robotics, automation and artificial intelligence commission, license high-risk AI systems, and create a cryptocurrency and blockchain study task force.
